rounds.proof_sketch: When dilation=1: (x + 1 - 1)/1 = x and (x + 1 - 1)*1 = x. Both expressions evaluate identically. The mutation only produces different results when dilation > 1, which requires changing model initialization parameters, not input values.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes division by dilation to multiplication by dilation in the calculation of last_valid_k. However, when dilation=1 (the default and apparently configured value), both (n)/1 and (n)*1 equal n. Layer 2's 112 rounds of bitwise equivalence across diverse value patterns confirms this. The model's dilation parameter is set at construction time and cannot be influenced by input tensor values. Since the testing contract allows only value changes to fixed-shape inputs, the mutation is semantically equivalent under this configuration.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable under fixed configuration. Would require changing model's dilation parameter to >1, which violates the fixed-shape contract that includes fixed model parameters.
rounds.recommendations: For mutation testing coverage, parameterize tests to exercise non-default configurations (dilation>1) since mutations in configuration-dependent code paths are only testable when those configurations are active. Consider adding explicit test cases for dilation=2 or higher to the test suite.
